clue.text: Put out the salty secret

indicators.note: something put out is disturbed or knocked out of place, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has been told to throw away a secret stash of salty food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' sounds like an order to discard something, but it signals that THE and SALTY are jumbled together.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy means done furtively, out of sight, the way a secret action is carried out.

clue.text: Show up Censor in separate notes

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the show's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Cats is a long-running stage musical
Cato the Elder, the Roman statesman, was known as Cato the Censor

explanation.surface: A censor turns up and exposes a musical passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show up' reads as expose; it is a musical, CATS, reversed. Cato held the Roman office of censor.
explanation.definitionFit: Staccato is a musical direction meaning each note is played short and detached from the next.

clue.text: Another telephone? Next one is different

indicators.note: different tells you the letters take another form, a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Ordering a second phone, someone finds the next one is not the same.
explanation.definitionFit: An extension is an additional phone line connected to the same main number.

clue.text: One is not confined at this comprehensive

definitions.text: One is not confined at this

explanation.surface: A school where pupils run free.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone at large is free, not locked up, and large also means broad or wide-ranging in scope.

clue.text: Electors from here transfer no money

indicators.note: no means the coin letter has to be left out

parts.note: to hand over is to transfer
D is the abbreviation for an old penny, a piece of money

explanation.surface: Voters from this place transfer no cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Electors were the German princes who chose the Holy Roman Emperor; the Elector of Hanover became Britain's George I. D is the old British penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanover was ruled by Electors, princes with a vote in choosing the Holy Roman Emperor.

clue.text: Mischievous child in an awkward situation

explanation.surface: A naughty youngster finds themselves in a tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A little pickle is a playful word for a rascal of a child, and being in a pickle means being in a fix or predicament.

clue.text: Reformed sinner has not retired

indicators.note: reformed means formed anew, so these letters are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A reformed sinner is still working.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is an idiom from draught horses: in harness means still at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in harness is still working at their job, like a horse still yoked to its cart.

clue.text: Rise of the Protector under the King

indicators.note: in a down clue under puts the nickname below the king's letter

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
Old Noll was a nickname for Oliver Cromwell, Lord Protector

explanation.surface: Cromwell, the Lord Protector, rises up beneath a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Noll is an old pet form of Oliver, used mockingly of Cromwell.
explanation.definitionFit: A knoll is a small rounded hill, a rise in the land.

clue.text: Girl who kept a diary?

explanation.surface: A question about a girl who wrote a journal.
explanation.definitionFit: Evelyn is a female first name, and John Evelyn was the seventeenth-century diarist, a contemporary of Pepys.

clue.text: City without a working gaol

indicators.note: without means the letter a is removed from the city

parts.note: Paris is the French capital city
on means operating or working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A town with no functioning jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A prison is a place of detention; gaol is the British spelling of jail.

clue.text: To rear nameless flower

indicators.note: N is the standard abbreviation for name, and being nameless means that letter has to go

parts.note: astern means towards the back of a ship, to the rear

explanation.surface: An instruction to grow a flower with no name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To rear' looks like a verb meaning raise, as a gardener rears plants; it is the nautical sense, ASTERN, and 'nameless' drops its N.
explanation.definitionFit: The aster is a daisy-like garden flower, such as the Michaelmas daisy.

clue.text: Prime Minister Paderewski, for instance, attracts 16

parts.note: Lord North was British Prime Minister during the American War of Independence
Ignacy Paderewski, the pianist and statesman, was a Pole

explanation.surface: A Polish premier draws in some figure numbered 16.
explanation.walkthrough: Paderewski was Prime Minister of Poland, which tempts you to keep the phrase together; Lord North is a separate prime minister. 16 is NEEDLE: a compass needle points to the magnetic north.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass needle swings towards the magnetic pole in the north, as if pulled there.

clue.text: Study China's revolutionary jams

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: revolutionary hints at turning round, so the porcelain's name is written in the opposite direction

parts.note: Sevres is a famous French porcelain, a kind of china

explanation.surface: Someone researches revolutionary China and its traffic jams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' reads as the country and 'revolutionary' as its politics; it is porcelain from Sevres, turned to SERVES.
explanation.definitionFit: Conserves are fruit preserves, a jam-like spread.

clue.text: Come round to mock

explanation.surface: Someone recovers only to be taunted.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally is to recover strength after illness, and in an older sense to rally someone is to tease or banter with them.

clue.text: Man prepared for action, turned and set off

indicators.note: turned means the joined man's name and girded word are read back to front together

parts.note: Reg is a man's name, short for Reginald
girt means girded, belted up ready for a fight

explanation.surface: A soldier, ready for battle, wheels round and marches off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses the whole run REG + GIRT, giving TRIG + GER.
explanation.definitionFit: To trigger something is to start it off or set it in motion, like an explosion.

clue.text: Salutation Sir Galahad possibly heard

indicators.note: heard means the phrase describing Galahad is spoken, and the words that sound the same are entered

parts.note: Sir Galahad, the purest of King Arthur's knights, is an example of a virtuous man of chivalry

explanation.surface: A greeting someone heard from Sir Galahad.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying goodnight is a farewell greeting given at the end of the day.

clue.text: Must the French be irritating?

parts.note: must means have to, need
le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: A question whether French people have to be so annoying.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle is to provoke or annoy someone with persistent small jibes.

clue.text: Relaxed with flowers, doubtless

parts.note: leis are Hawaiian garlands of flowers
surely means without doubt

explanation.surface: Someone takes it easy among flowers, without a doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisurely means unhurried and easy-going.

clue.text: For instance, doctors swallow initially four large iced drinks

parts.note: eg is short for exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: swallow means the doctors take the following letters into their middle

parts.note: GPs are general practitioners, family doctors

indicators.note: initially tells you to take the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Doctors, say, gulp four big cold drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'iced' seems to describe the drinks, but only its first letter is used: FLI goes inside GPS.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg flip is a drink of beaten egg with milk, beer or spirits, like eggnog.

clue.text: I love fellows — that's not to be repeated

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
love is a zero score in tennis, shaped like the letter O
F is an abbreviation for fellow, doubled to FF for the plural

explanation.surface: A declaration of love for men, made just once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' as nil in tennis gives O; 'fellows' gives FF, the doubled letter showing a plural as pp does for pages.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-off is a unique event that happens a single time and never again.

clue.text: Outspoken for an interval

annotationWithheld.why: Outspoken for an interval (6): FOURTH is FORTH (=out) said aloud, but the single word Outspoken must give both FORTH and the homophone signal, a word doing two jobs

clue.text: Don't start tilting and toppling

indicators.note: don't start tells you to leave off the first letter of the synonym

parts.note: tilting is charging with a lance at a joust

explanation.surface: A plea to stop leaning over before something falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tilting' looks like leaning; it is the medieval sport of jousting with lances, and losing its first letter leaves the word for overthrowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ousting is driving someone out of power, bringing them down as if knocked off a horse.

clue.text: Puts on a diversion, to release those 6

indicators.note: a diversion is a turning aside, so the letters are sent off in another order

explanation.surface: Someone stages an entertainment to free the horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is IN HARNESS; outspan is a South African word for unyoking draught animals.
explanation.definitionFit: To outspan is to unharness oxen or horses from a wagon.

clue.text: Pitched high for a good score at darts

explanation.surface: A high throw earns a good darts score.
explanation.definitionFit: Treble is the highest voice part in music, and the treble ring on a dartboard triples a throw's value.

clue.text: Good fellow, this murder victim

explanation.surface: A decent man turns out to be the one who was murdered.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Goodfellow is the mischievous sprite Puck of English folklore, and the nursery rhyme Who Killed Cock Robin tells of the bird's killing.

clue.text: Shrub is a sort of brush

explanation.surface: A bush that is a type of sweeping brush.
explanation.definitionFit: Broom is a yellow-flowered bush, and a broom is a long-handled sweeping tool, once made from that plant's twigs.

clue.text: Not easily deceived about tobacco

parts.note: up to can mean about, engaged in, as in what are you up to
snuff is powdered tobacco taken through the nose

explanation.surface: Someone sharp is wise to a story about tobacco.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is old slang: being up to snuff meant being knowing and sharp, not easily taken in.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone up to snuff is shrewd and alert, too knowing to be fooled.

clue.text: Log is rewritten in Irish port

indicators.note: rewritten means the letters are written out again in another order

explanation.surface: A ship's log is updated in an Irish harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sligo is a town and seaport on the north-west coast of Ireland.

clue.text: Raised black, shaggy sheep

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
shaggy means rough-coated
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A dark, woolly sheep has been reared on a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Brought up means reared or raised from childhood.

clue.text: In practice. Nigerians are a warlike tribe

indicators.note: in tells you the answer sits inside the words that follow, across the full stop

explanation.surface: Nigerians are said to be a fighting people when it comes to practice.
explanation.walkthrough: The full stop splits the run, but the letters run straight on across it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were the ancient British people led by Boudicca in revolt against Rome.

clue.text: Hatred of monstrous crime, when gold is stolen

indicators.note: is stolen means the gold is taken away from the crime word, leaving the rest

parts.note: an enormity is a monstrous wrong or atrocity
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Loathing aroused by an outrageous robbery of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a gold theft; in fact OR, heraldry's gold, is removed from ENORMITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Enmity is deep hostility or ill will between people.

clue.text: Mark handwritten words that mean the opposite

parts.note: Mark Antony, the Roman general
MS stands for manuscript, a handwritten document

explanation.surface: Someone notes down by hand some words of contrary meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a verb (write a mark); it is Mark Antony's first name, leading to his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonyms are pairs of words with contrary meanings, such as hot and cold.
